content:
**Visual observations from test image:**
- Open/split soybean pod showing seeds inside
- One seed at top appears pale/whitish and cottony in texture
- Middle seed shows white fuzzy/cottony fungal growth
- Lower seeds appear dark brown to black, shrunken/shriveled
- Pod wall itself is brown/mature

**Reasoning:**
- The white cottony/crusty fungal growth inside the pod directly on seeds strongly matches **Downy mildew**: *"the inside of the pod and seed may be covered with a dried, whitish fungal mass that appears crusty and contains spores. Infected seeds can be smaller, appear dull white, and have cracks in the seed coat."*
- White Mold reference shows primarily stem/canopy symptoms; the seed-interior pod symptom shown here doesn't match as well
- Phomopsis also shows chalky white mold on seeds, but primarily describes cracked/shriveled seeds with reddish-brown streaks on stems
- The white cottony material directly inside the pod cavity on the seeds is the most distinctive feature here, and it aligns best with Downy mildew's pod interior fungal mass description
